A fetch Response lacks those properties, so when credential sync is enabled the HubSpot refresh path misbehaves (undefined fields, bad expiry, schema parse failure) — a real type/behavior mismatch introduced by this diff.

judged_text: In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code assigns it to hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken and the following code reads .expires_in/.access_token directly off it — properties a fetch Response does not have. hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in is undefined so the expiry is computed as NaN and hubspotCredentialSchema.parse throws on the Response object (which lacks every HubspotToken field), so HubSpot token refresh always fails whenever sync is enabled and HubSpot operations requiring a fresh token break.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result of `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is assigned to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken`, i.e. the calling code is written as if it receives a HubSpot token payload object rather than a `Response`. This is a real behavioral mismatch introduced by the diff: in sync mode the returned value will not have HubSpot token fields (it will be a `Response`), so downstream access to token properties would break.
